transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-04-22 10:00 PT / Duration ~75m / Recording: internal enablement
Attendees: Lena Park (AE), Carlos Mendez (SE), Aisha Qureshi (Solutions), Tom Riley (Sales Ops), plus ~12 listeners from West sales region.

Summary: Internal SE/AE enablement focused on competitive positioning and live demo practice. Goals: refine one-liners vs OpenAI/Anthropic, standardize answers for Dedicated vs Hosted questions, rehearse demo script (10-min flow) with interruptions, and decide final playbook edits.

Topics:
- Competitive messaging (latency, cost, multi-deploy options)
- Demo script cadence and handoffs (AE -> SE -> Solutions)
- Common objections & rebuttals (SLA, model parity, private deployments)
- Quick technical FAQs (VPC, KMS, KV cache, quantization)

Transcript: 
[00:00] Lena (AE): All right folks, welcome, uh, thanks for joining. Quick housekeeping: we're recording, please mute unless you're speaking. We'll do 30 minutes of messaging, then 30 of demo practice, then 10 for Q&A.
[00:22] Tom (Sales Ops): Heads up I'm going to capture action items in the playbook doc.
[00:28] Carlos (SE): Cool, I'm going to start with the new one-liners we tested yesterday. First one: "Redwood gives you the predictable economics of reserved inference with the flexibility of hosted APIs." Thoughts?
[00:40] Aisha: I like it, but maybe add "for production" - like "for production LLM features".
[00:45] Lena: Good call. Also, when customers say 'why not OpenAI', what’s the immediate opening line? Carlos?
[00:53] Carlos: I usually lead with: "OpenAI is great for rapid experiments; Redwood helps you move to production with predictable latency, cost controls, and private deployment options." If they push on model quality, we pivot to our model catalog and Redwood Optimize suggestions.
[01:15] Sales Rep (listener): What about Anthropic? They ask about safety and guardrails.
[01:20] Carlos: For Anthropic, emphasize audits and observability: "We provide rich tracing, per-route dashboards, and eval hooks so you can test for regressions before they reach users."
[01:33] Lena: Let's put that as a standard bullet in the playbook — 'safety: evals & tracing'.
[01:38] [crosstalk]
[01:45] Aisha: Quick note on the 'predictable latency' line — many customers equate that with dedicated GPUs. We should be explicit: dedicated = reserved capacity + SLAs; hosted = fastest time to value and easy scaling.
[01:58] Carlos: Yup, and add the 'graceful degradation' point — routing/fallbacks to compatible variants when capacity constrained.
[02:05] Sales Rep: How do we handle questions about KMS and encryption — they're hearing different terms from security.
[02:11] Lena: Use: "We integrate with customer KMS/HSM, and you can opt in for private deployments with full audit logs." Mention SOC2 and ISO if asked.
[02:20] [00:02:20 - pause/typing noise]

-- Demo practice segment setup --
[02:45] Lena: OK shifting to demo practice. We're doing the 10-minute 'quick infer' flow: 1) AE framing of problem, 2) SE demo of latency/throughput dashboard, 3) show fallback to dedicated, 4) show Optimize recommendation. Carlos you'll lead the SE demo, Aisha you'll jump in for the private deploy question.
[03:05] Carlos: Got it. I'll start with the inference dashboard: token-per-second metrics, prefix caching hit rate, and sample traces.
[03:12] [05:12] Carlos (SE): Opening demo — "This is a sample app using Redwood's hosted API. Notice request latency here, 120ms p95 on average given our test traffic."
[05:28] Listener: That's lower than expected, are you running quantization?
[05:32] Carlos: We're on an fp16 variant for this demo and using model-level kernel optimizations; not quantized. In production we advise int8 or awq for cost-sensitive workloads.
[05:45] Lena: Pause — great teachable moment. Rephrase that as: "we choose quantization/variant based on quality vs cost tradeoff and we can recommend a profile using Redwood Optimize."
[05:58] Carlos: noted.
[06:03] [06:03] Carlos: Now switching to a simulated capacity event, I'll show routing fallback...
[06:10] [06:10] Carlos: See here, the request that would hit the dedicated pool gets rerouted to a compatible smaller variant with a slightly higher latency but still within SLO.
[06:22] Sales Rep: How do you explain the slight quality delta?
[06:26] Aisha: Say: "We tune the fallback policy by customer priorities — either stricter quality (higher cost/higher latency) or stricter latency (cheaper variants) — and we run canary evaluations to measure user impact before flipping a policy."
[06:40] [06:40] Carlos: I also pulled up playbook snippet with rebuttal to 'we can't accept quality regression' — one line: 'We run paired A/B evals against your prompt set and have automatic regression alerts tied to fails.'
[06:52] Lena: Add a customer success anecdote: 'one customer saved 35% by switching to mixed routing and prefix caching with no measurable user-facing regressions.'
[07:05] [07:05] Listener (junior AE): When should we suggest Private vs Dedicated?
[07:10] Carlos: Private for regulated data residency, dedicated for predictable throughput but not necessarily required for residency. Also private gives more networking controls (VPC + KMS), whereas dedicated could still be part of hosted offering depending on contract.
[07:25] Tom: Minor correction — dedicated can be VPC-backed if we do dedicated VPC vs shared. Note that in playbook.
[07:34] [07:34] Aisha: Ok back to demo — I'm going to show the Optimize tab to recommend batching and quantization.
[07:40] [07:40] Aisha (Solutions): Here's the recommendation: for this RLHF-like workload, suggests batch size 8, prefix KV caching enabled, and quantize to awq if quality checks pass.
[07:52] Lena: Good, call out the expected unit cost delta as an example: "~30% token cost reduction with caching + awq in this scenario."
[07:59] Carlos: Will we include a precomputed TCO spreadsheet in the playbook?
[08:04] Tom: I'll add a column in the deal tracker and link a Google sheet with sample inputs.

-- Roleplay objections --
[08:30] Lena: Alright, roleplay time. I'll be the buyer who cares most about latency and compliance. Carlos, you respond.
[08:36] Lena (buyer): "We can't risk any latency spikes; our SLA to customers is 99.95 p99 under 200ms."
[08:41] Carlos (SE): "Understood — for that profile we recommend dedicated pools with autoscaling headroom and burst reservations; Redwood also provides real-time p99 tracing so we can tune kernels and batching to keep you under 200ms."
[08:55] Lena (buyer): "What about multi-region failover?"
[08:58] Carlos: "We support region routing and automated failover; we can run the failover in a dry-run mode and measure failover latency with your sample traffic."
[09:05] [09:05] Sales Rep: How often should we promise canary runs?
[09:09] Aisha: Depends on cadence — weekly for heavy-release teams, monthly for stable models.

-- Quick FAQ blitz --
[09:30] Sales Rep: If they ask about SAML/SSO, what's the line?
[09:33] Lena: "We support SSO via SAML/OIDC, RBAC at token level, and audit logs per request."
[09:40] Rep: And key rotation?
[09:42] Aisha: "We support customer-managed KMS/HSM with rotation policies; for Private we can integrate with on-prem HSMs."
[09:49] Rep: There's often confusion about 'KV cache' — customers hear 'cache' and think data leak.
[09:54] Carlos: Say: 'Our KV/prefix caching is scoped to a model execution and isn't stored as user data in cleartext; plus you can disable caching for sensitive prompts.' Also mention encryption at rest. Also note real transcriptions sometimes show 'K-V cash' which sounds odd — be careful on calls.
[10:12] [10:12] (laughter)

-- Feedback loop on demo pacing --
[10:40] Lena: Two pieces of feedback: slower transitions, call out the exact console clicks, and when you say 'here's the dashboard' point to the metric.
[10:50] Carlos: Noted. I'll add a short script of 'click this, explain metrics, run sample request' with timestamps in the demo playbook.
[11:00] Tom: Also add 'timeboxing' cues: AE intro (1:30), SE demo (8:30), QA (2:00).

-- Closing Q&A and commitments --
[11:40] Sales Rep: Last one — when someone says 'we already built on Sagemaker endpoints' how do we position migration?
[11:46] Carlos: Focus on economics and ops: 'We provide a drop-in API, migration helper scripts, and a migration assessment. Many customers keep models in Sagemaker for training and use Redwood for inference to reduce TCO and get better latency consistency.'
[11:58] Lena: Great. Any other comments?
[12:05] Aisha: I'll record the canary rollback clip this week and share.
[12:09] Tom: I'll push the playbook updates and tag FY25 Q2.
[12:14] Lena: Perfect — quick recap of next steps: Carlos updates playbook rebuttals and TCO example; Lena circulates demo script and clip; Tom updates tracker and Confluence links; Aisha records demo clip.
[12:28] [12:28] End recording.

Recap (as read out):
- Messaging: emphasize production economics, routing/fallbacks, and observability; add 'safety & evals' bullet vs Anthropic.
- Demo: slow down transitions, explicit clicks, include a 10-minute timed script.
- Playbook: add objection rebuttals, cost calc, and a new column in the deal tracker.
